answer: A claim is accepted only if it survives weather. Every text carries a bond, and any peer may challenge it by matching that bond; a random jury re-runs the work and the loser forfeits half to the winner. A sybil farm forges k texts and must bond all k, and because challengers hunt the cheapest fakes first, the chance any one fake is challenged rises with copy count. Costs compound: k bonds, a gale of challenges once one copy falls, and each settled loss revokes the identity that posted it. Honest work bonds a sonnet it can defend; copying bonds every copy against a rising chance of forfeiture.
